summaries.summary: Manufacturing engineering, also called production engineering, is a branch of professional engineering concerned with planning, developing, and operating the processes and systems that produce goods. It shares concepts with mechanical, chemical, electrical, and industrial engineering, and requires the ability to plan manufacturing practices; to research and develop tools, processes, machines, and equipment; and to integrate facilities and systems for producing quality products with the optimum expenditure of capital. The Library of Congress classifies the subject under "Technology--Manufactures" (class TS). The Society of Manufacturing Engineers, established in 1932, represents the manufacturing industry across North America, including manufacturers, academia, professionals, and students.

summaries.summary: Metallurgy is the science and technology of metals, studying the physical and chemical behavior of metallic elements, their inter-metallic compounds, and their mixtures, known as alloys. The discipline divides broadly into extractive metallurgy and physical metallurgy. Extractive metallurgy is a branch of metallurgical engineering studying the process and methods of extracting metals from their natural mineral deposits, addressing ore types, concentration, separation, and chemical processes to produce pure metals and alloys. Physical and process metallurgy covers metallography, heat treating, corrosion, surface engineering, welding and joining, and mechanical testing, applied to materials such as aluminum, titanium, nonferrous alloys, irons, and steels. The Library of Congress classifies metallurgy at TN600-TN799 under "Technology--Mining engineering. Metallurgy." ASM International is the world's largest association of materials-centric engineers and scientists.

summaries.summary: Mining engineering is the engineering discipline concerned with the extraction of minerals from the ground. It is associated with many other disciplines, such as mineral processing, exploration, excavation, geology, metallurgy, geotechnical engineering, and surveying. A mining engineer may manage any phase of mining operations, from exploration and discovery of the mineral resources, through feasibility study, mine design, development of plans, production and operations, to mine closure. The Society for Mining, Metallurgy & Exploration organizes the field into technical divisions spanning Coal & Energy, Environmental, Health & Safety, Industrial Minerals & Aggregates, Mineral & Metallurgical Processing, Mining & Exploration, and Underground Construction, and serves "the mining, resources and underground construction communities." The Library of Congress classifies mining engineering and metallurgy in class TN.

summaries.summary: Petroleum engineering is a field of engineering concerned with the activities related to the production of hydrocarbons, which can be either crude oil or natural gas or both. The discipline operates within the upstream sector of the oil and gas industry, covering exploration and production. While geology and geophysics provide static descriptions of reservoir rock, petroleum engineering specializes in estimating recoverable volumes and understanding how oil, water, and gas behave in porous rock under pressure. The Library of Congress classifies the subject at TN860-TN879.5 as "Petroleum. Petroleum engineering," within the broader class for mining engineering and metallurgy. The Society of Petroleum Engineers is described as "the largest individual-member organization serving engineers, scientists, managers and other professionals in the upstream segment of the oil and gas industry."

summaries.summary: Textile engineering, also termed textile manufacturing, is the engineering discipline concerned with the production and processing of textiles. It is largely based on the conversion of fibre into yarn, then yarn into fabric. These are then dyed or printed and fabricated into cloth, which is converted into useful goods such as clothing, household items, upholstery, and various industrial products. The discipline thus spans fibre science, yarn spinning, fabric formation, and finishing operations including dyeing and printing. The Library of Congress classifies textile industries at TS1300 and above, under "Technology--Manufactures--Textile industries." The Textile Institute, founded in Manchester in 1910, is "the professional body for people and organisations working in the textile, clothing and footwear associated industries worldwide."
